title: Krichevsky–Trofimov potential at the two coin endpoints

source.book: Francesco Orabona, Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization, v10
locations: Theorem 13.4 proof, printed 210 / PDF 222 (ε-scaled potential, initial value and endpoint update).

definition:
noncomputable def ktPotential (ε : ℝ) (t : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ε * (2 : ℝ)^t * Real.Gamma (((t : ℝ) + 1 + x) / 2) *
    Real.Gamma (((t : ℝ) + 1 - x) / 2) /
      (Real.pi * Real.Gamma ((t : ℝ) + 1))
headers:
theorem ktPotential_initial (ε : ℝ) :
    ktPotential ε 0 0 = ε

theorem ktPotential_endpoint (ε : ℝ) (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t)
    (x c : ℝ) (hx : |x| ≤ (t : ℝ) - 1) (hc : c = -1 ∨ c = 1) :
    ktPotential ε t (x + c) = (1 + c * x / (t : ℝ)) * ktPotential ε (t - 1) x
relation: The printed argument uses t≥1, |x|≤t−1 and c∈{−1,1}. These imply |x+c|≤t and both prior Gamma arguments (t±x)/2≥1/2, including t=1,x=0. Lean represents the formula on all real x; the recurrence asserts an identity on the printed carrier. Both equalities extend to every real scale ε by homogeneity; the bettor starts with strictly positive wealth.
proof: At t=0, Γ(1/2)=√π and Γ(1)=1 give F₀(0)=ε. Moving from t−1 to t doubles 2^(t−1) and changes Γ(t) to tΓ(t). The right coin increments only (t+x)/2; the left coin increments only (t−x)/2. Gamma recurrence gives factors 1+x/t and 1−x/t. All denominator cancellation uses t>0, π>0, and Γ(t)>0.
consumer_headers:
theorem fractional_history_two_outcomes :
    ktPotential 1 3 (3/2) = (7/6 : ℝ) * ktPotential 1 2 (1/2) ∧
    ktPotential 1 3 (-(1/2)) = (5/6 : ℝ) * ktPotential 1 2 (1/2) ∧
    0 < ktPotential 1 3 (-(1/2)) ∧
    ktPotential 1 3 (-(1/2)) < ktPotential 1 3 (3/2)
consumer_meaning: At t=1 both outcomes preserve initial wealth 7. At t=3 and real prior history x=1/2 the two factors are 7/6 and 5/6, with strictly different positive outcomes.
remaining_source_obligations: Interior coin inequality (13.1) for −1<c<1 via log-convexity and interpolation
Second exponential lower bound and A.13 dependency
